`v0.14.0` ships Wau OS inside the Omarchy guest. The guest image now installs Wau OS from a verified package, so a fresh Windows host boots into an Omarchy desktop that already has Wau OS configured, instead of one that needs Wau OS installed afterwards.

# Features

* The factory guest image installs Wau OS (`herald-os-bin 0.1.0alpha.5-1`) from a reviewed, digest-verified package. The package is added to the guest's locked transaction after the package install, so the image never resolves an unreviewed package from a live repository.
* The guest's first-run provisioning gains a "set up Wau OS" step. It runs with the rest of the first-run steps and is optional: the step says so and exits when Wau OS is not installed.
* Wau OS and its compositor dependencies (`niri`, `swaybg`, `swaylock`) are part of the reviewed guest package lock, and the factory image grows to 10240 MiB to hold them.

## Dev

* Compress the guest image inside the launcher's decoder window. The launcher reads the frame with a window of at most 512 MiB, so 29 is the largest window it can decode; the previous 256 MiB window stored the repeated local package archives more than once and pushed the release asset past GitHub's 2 GiB per-asset limit.
* Store each local package archive once in the factory image. The update offer and the live local repository carry the same archive bytes, and the image now links them instead of copying them.
* Refresh the guest package lock for the packages that changed while the Wau OS guest was assembled.
